$comment: What this repository contributes to a running stack, and what a check may
believe about it. `checked` is proved against this repository by
internal/manifest/manifest_test.go in this repository's own CI; `declared` is
a statement nobody can verify and carries its own `why`.
TWO COMPONENTS, ONE BINARY. estate.json says this repository runs `idryx` and
`idryx-detect`, and there is one package: they are two SUBCOMMANDS of it.
That is the fourth shape this schema has had to carry, after service, tool
and daemon, and it is why `subcommand` exists as a checked field. A manifest
that gave each component its own package would have had to invent one.
THE PAIR IS THE FIFTH. `IDRYX_TRUST_DOMAIN` is not optional and not required:
it is required IF AND ONLY IF `IDRYX_EVENTS` is set, because the envelope
wants agent://<trust-domain>/<name> and only the operator can say the domain.
A `required: true/false` field cannot express that, so it is a checked fact of
its own, proved by running the binary three ways.
AND ONE FACT WORTH READING BEFORE ANYBODY EXPOSES THIS. Nothing here
authenticates. /healthz and /api/identities both answer 200 with no
credential, which is correct for a read-only dashboard whose default bind is
loopback, and is the OPPOSITE of wardryx, where every /v1 route answers 401
without a key. Containment is the deployment's job and both server
deployments do it: stack-single publishes no port for it and stack-k8s gives
it a ClusterIP Service with no type. Declared here so that the day somebody
adds an ingress, the property they are changing is written down rather than
assumed.

the_deployments_bind_it_wider_on_purpose.why: The declared default is loopback, and both server deployments pass --addr 0.0.0.0:8081 because a container or pod reaches its peers on no other interface. Neither publishes it outward: stack-single gives the service no `ports:` key at all and stack-k8s's Service has no `type`, so it is ClusterIP. The bind is wider and the reach is not.

it_is_the_scheduled_half.why: stack-up runs it at :37 past and stack-k8s as a CronJob, both as a fresh pass over the same event log the serving idryx reads. The name in estate.json's `runs` is the ROUTINE's name, not a binary's, which is why it maps to a subcommand here.

pairs.why: idryx inventories identities under its own short ids and the envelope wants agent://<trust-domain>/<name>. Only the operator can say the domain, so it refuses rather than inventing one.
